step1_figure.circuit_type: CMFB Amplifiers (Diode-Connected Load vs. Current-Mirror Load Diff-Amps)
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.28 shows the two common-mode feedback (CMFB) differential amplifier topologies evaluated for the fully-differential op-amp: (a) a PMOS differential pair with diode-connected NMOS loads exhibiting gain < 1, and (b) a PMOS differential pair with an NMOS current-mirror load providing a gain of approximately 8.

gain_diode_load.description: Voltage gain d(VCMFB1)/d(VCMA) of the diode-connected load CMFB differential amplifier

equation.formula: A_v1 = g_mp / (g_mn + g_dsp + g_dsn) \approx g_mp / g_mn = \sqrt{\frac{\mu_p C_{ox} (W/L)_p}{\mu_n C_{ox} (W/L)_n}}
equation.explanation: The gain of a differential pair with diode-connected load is roughly the ratio of the transconductances of the input PMOS pair and NMOS load devices.
equation.assumptions: Both transistors are in saturation; channel length modulation g_ds << g_m.

sky130_expected.calculation: With (W/L)_p = 20/1, (W/L)_n = 10/1, mu_p*Cox = 50 uA/V^2, mu_n*Cox = 270 uA/V^2: A_v1 ≈ sqrt((50 * 20) / (270 * 10)) = sqrt(1000 / 2700) = sqrt(0.37) ≈ 0.61 V/V. Including output conductances (gds ≈ 0.1*Id), gain reduces to approximately 0.4 - 0.55 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker explicitly notes in Fig 26.28(a) and the text that this gain is considerably less than 1 (around 0.3 to 0.6 V/V).

gain_mirror_load.description: Voltage gain d(VCMFB2)/d(VCMA) of the current-mirror load CMFB differential amplifier

equation.explanation: The differential-to-single-ended current mirror loaded PMOS diff-pair provides full gm*ro voltage gain.
equation.assumptions: Output node has high impedance loaded only by the drain resistances of xm9 (PMOS) and xm6 (NMOS).

sky130_expected.calculation: For I_D = 10 uA per branch, (W/L)_p = 20/1: g_mp = sqrt(2 * 50u * 20 * 10u) = 141 uA/V. r_on = 1 / (0.1 * 10u) = 1 MOhm, r_op = 1 / (0.1 * 10u) = 1 MOhm. r_out = 500 kOhm. Ideal A_v2 = 141 uA/V * 500 kOhm ≈ 70. However, at lower Vds near the boundaries of saturation and short channel effects, effective ro is reduced, giving a gain of 8 to 25 V/V (Baker reports ~8).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker text on p. 882 states: 'Using the diff-amp with current mirror load, Fig. 26.28b, gives a gain of approximately 8'.

vcmfb1_quiescent.description: Output voltage VCMFB1 of the diode-load CMFB amplifier when VCMA = VCM = 500 mV

equation.explanation: Since xm6t is diode-connected to ground, its drain voltage is simply its Vgs at branch current Id = I_tail / 2.
equation.assumptions: Symmetrical differential pair with equal current split at VCMA = VCM.

sky130_expected.calculation: For I_D ≈ 10 uA, Vthn = 0.42 V, mu_n*Cox = 270 uA/V^2, (W/L)_n = 10/1: Vov = sqrt(2 * 10u / (270u * 10)) = sqrt(20 / 2700) ≈ 0.086 V. V_CMFB1 = 0.42 + 0.086 ≈ 0.506 V (in 1V/Baker technology it is ~320 mV).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker shows VCMFB1 around 320 mV at VCMA=500 mV in Fig 26.28a, noting it is too low to properly bias the op-amp's CMFB control device.

vcmfb2_quiescent.description: Output voltage VCMFB2 of the current-mirror CMFB amplifier when VCMA = VCM = 500 mV

equation.explanation: At balanced input, the output sits at the high-gain transition midpoint required to properly bias the NMOS control device in the op-amp.
equation.assumptions: Matching between current mirror transistors xm7 and xm6.

sky130_expected.calculation: At VCMA = VCM = 500 mV, the currents through xm8 and xm9 are equal, matching the mirrored current from xm7 to xm6. The output settles in the high-gain region between 350 mV and 600 mV, matching the required ~400 mV bias point.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As stated on p. 882: 'As seen in Fig. 26.27, we need approximately 400 mV'.

cmfb_loop_gain.description: Total CMFB loop gain combining the CMFB amplifier and op-amp CMFB path (A_opamp ≈ 25)

equation.explanation: The overall common-mode loop gain is the product of the CMFB error amplifier gain and the gain from VCMFB to the differential amplifier outputs.

sky130_expected.calculation: With A_v2 ≈ 8 and op-amp internal CMFB gain of ~25: A_loop = 8 * 25 = 200.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker explicitly derives: 'This combined with the op-amp\'s CMFB gain gives an overall CMFB loop gain of 200'.

step3_testbench.description: DC sweep testbench measuring the transfer curves and voltage gains of both CMFB amplifiers (diode-load and current-mirror load) as shown in Fig. 26.28.
